notes.title: Dev Insights: Nala's Parents
notes.content:
At one point in the game, the world collapses and Nala begins to reminisce about her own memories.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/9d5a472ecf49f34df133f79cafa1bde07d58b3a8.png
Memories of the Family

The memories of her parents were vague, so we portrayed them using shadow puppets inspired by Indonesian performance Wayang Kulit which literally translates to "Skin Puppet." We felt this medium could somehow convey deep emotions even with abstract and less detailed visuals.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/7d3a283247089213b27e2ba4e8ce06c689b224d8.jpgWayang Kulit (The Jakarta Post/Stefanus Ajie)

The performance usually brings ancient tales, memories of the past, which in this case is Nala's family. We drew from that inspiration, simplified it, and reshaped it as if told out of a children's book. The style resonates with the visuals of Nala's childhood book, Echo, which her mother often read to her when she was around.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/d4696f1e9e892187a1e21eab978b5bdc0dd4e3a3.png  {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/8ba319a9e57966705bc76cce0aa9a69a2217639f.png

Nala was born into a warm, loving family. As an only child, she was cherished by her parents and grandparents. Her early years were filled with laughter, stories, and love. But everything changed when she was five. Her parents left her without warning, and not long later, her grandmother passed away. From that point on, Nala lived alone with her grandfather.

Grief had hollowed her grandfather. Though he tried to care for Nala, his heart was broken, and the emotional warmth she needed slowly faded. He provided, but he couldn't always be present. And Nala, still so young, didn't understand why the love around her had gone quiet. She grew up feeling alone, unloved even. While her friends spoke of being pampered by their parents, Nala listened in silence, carrying a quiet jealousy she never dared to voice.

Chasing What Fades

As the perspective shifts, we invite players not only to explore those memories but to live them in first person.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/2f1e7d61f72b170ee84eb2d1eda9f6f64115f7eb.png
As a teenager, Nala's loneliness deepened. She kept chasing the feeling of being loved, desperate for connection, but it always seemed just out of reach. Slowly, she began to realize, everyone she once felt close to seemed to drift away. First her parents, then her grandfather, who had never quite recovered from losing his wife. With no one else to blame, Nala turned inward. She blamed herself.

It's been so long since she felt parental love that sometimes she forgets what her parents looked like. She has to study old photographs just to remember their faces.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/c28d4a796f804dfefcda0a819a5af85875c30384.png

notes.title: Dev Insights: Nala
notes.content:
Nala is the main protagonist of this story. When we created her, we wanted her to represent someone shaped by a heavy past, a series of seemingly simple events that gradually built into something complex enough to leave gaps in her memory, filling her with regret that suppressed her personality and emotions, fracturing her identity.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/f1c66616c20cb249443475eccaf75c103e42bfb2.gif

Characterization

Her story revolves around her biggest regret and the heavy burden of living with the thought that she killed her own grandfather in the past. She can't recall the details of what happened, but she remembers clearly holding her grandfather's cold body in her little arms.

Nala was an intellectual and creative girl. Now working as a scientist under her foster father, she has detached herself from that creative side because of her trauma. She subconsciously suppresses her emotions. Most of the time she remains calm, passive, and "normal." As a grown-up, she only does what needs to be done, making sure none of her past self ever surfaces.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/5e6d2f2e1c2b9da63a72309207a25c80be7f5ce7.png
Nala's family has all left her in one way or another. The only person she holds very dear now is her foster father, Toga, who took her in after she lost her grandfather. Since then, she has been a kind and obedient daughter to him, working together as a scientist.

Nala is a kind and caring woman. She's also a very hardworking person, very dedicated to her work, sometimes to a fault, prioritizing what her foster father wants before anything.

Visual Concept

Nala's design reflects her simple & straightforward nature and hardworking personality. The green tint in her hair is a trace of her past.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/762121cd1f194360ac2db106ebf6b7390a5fe4da.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/b6062dac3b727ed25d1bc5296bc2bf837de9ec6f.png

notes.title: Dev Insights: Dark World
notes.content:
The Dark World serves as a blank space, acting almost like a gate or a bridge that must be passed through before The Flower guides the way into The Memory World, but only if she allows it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/c9c2878862377f9603f389092736f777af5a1b59.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/3b26ec353f26dd93592164257fee03d7e0cae012.jpg

It is also the space where conversations with The Statue of Memories take place. The simulation of a new memory occurs there as well, before returning to The Memory World to observe the outcome.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/dbea48e9b8efb9b7fe71560f8965c12f30de190a.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/263ca0d6c4991da290b43b35e92986f75bf01691.png

Visual Concept

The surface of the ground is a liquid, with crystal shards underneath that come from The Flower's body. It's proof of how many times The Flower has tried and failed to simulate new changes to Nala's Memory.

White cords stretch down from the sky gripping the statue tightly, representing the pain of being bound by dark memories. They pinch and pull, as if trying to hold back any movement toward change.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/9381dbc08ac7d183b238efb5d73ef213626ae4f9.png

notes.title: Dev Insights: The Flower
notes.content:
The Flower is a mysterious being that owns the Memory World. The center of every visualization in Undying Flower. She has the ability to travel between memories of people.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/a020cf0f02d9ec43c7b3972cb8f8e6966510b014.gif

Visual Concept

We wanted her character to be mysterious, haunting yet beautiful, intensely emotional at times yet stoic at others. Every bit of her visualization showed that she is bound by something, but also symbolizes a ruler of a lonely world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/91e20035d85ef0e4a16e039c4b59b57d7b00d50d.png

As The Flower moves around in Memory World, players might notice a red, orb-like light glowing from within her heart. It highlights the human side of The Flower, suggesting that her emotions are still there, a different perspective where her soul looks detached previously in real world.

Her white transparent robe represents her innocent side as a little girl, covering her black body due to her being part of an abstraction of memory.

She wears a mask to cover her real face, yet she can express emotions through it. Her crown represents her rule over her own world, and yet, her neck and feet are bound by black thorny vines. The Flower appears all-powerful in her world, but desperate to be free. This visualization is inspired by Christ's crown of thorns.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/9b80214b9a1b4260947f9766159d7796e8600332.jpg {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/64be0abbc1ff98730fa911822fe360413f1058b6.jpg
Christ with the crown of thorns, as painted by Andrea Solario, 1513 (left) and El Greco, c.1580s (right)

More Than a Subject

The Flower represents the deepest, most suppressed part of the experimental subject as a young little girl. It is why she has no voice, but she uses something similar to a sign language to express words that only the people that she "invited" to her world can understand.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/9aeae167cc026d83836c2e1fe2b515cc6d965902.png
She has traveled through the memories of many people, and is now trapped in Nala's darkest memory. Her purpose remains a mystery, but her current mission is to change the outcome of Nala's regret to free her own soul and continue her journey.

She has tried to get out, desperately tried to change the outcome several times on her own, but turns out she couldn't do it on her own. So she "brought" Nala's soul with her to help.

notes.title: Dev Insights: Hospital
notes.content:
This is a sequence where The Flower is introduced as the subject of the experiment. Subject X02, Codename: The Flower, is a human test subject that is believed to have the power they need to erase a regret, a power to visit a memory and alter it. Nala has been caring for her as part of her tasks as a scientist working under her foster father, Toga.

The Hospital Room Scene
This scene captures the moment just before the experiment begins, a moment of unease where Nala's nightmare also takes place. The silent and dimly lit room portrays the atmosphere of emotional weight.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/6d6d766a9d6b6af2a7ddfdcc219c8e41205b1cc6.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/41345efbdb752507ef0969802cb95f9bbd3dfacc.jpg"]
The Flower appears as a frail little girl, barely alive. Her breath is her sign as a still-living being, yet her soul feels detached.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/09ac18135481b2f489dc6b0c32e042fd3a08b1c2.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/43a71814f2fd7446440441705a95f21d66e9ecbe.jpg"]
The Corridor Scene
This scene is designed to feel both real and surreal, a space where The Flower's involvement starts foreshadowing in Nala's consciousness. It's an anticipation of what is to come once the experiment begins.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/813f0bd22e12ca06733b759c99f701665cae335b.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/1259e47549bc8509c8ab0eb0a439565570f5a8d9.jpg"]

notes.title: Dev Insights: The Graveyard
notes.content:
A graveyard, a resting place of our beloved ones. It reminds us of certain important memories, both good and bad.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/f3953f5d0c1f58ae26e74c7432403aa9fa298391.png
The first graveyard scene is a visualization of Nala's recurring nightmare. For as long as she can remember, she has been haunted by her trauma, the feeling of guilt about her grandpa's death, and the uneasiness of not being able to remember what happened in her past.

A Chance
The presence of the aurora and the statue of Nala with a mask hint at the influence of The Flower, hidden behind the memories in Nala's past.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/de324dbdaa0067791b2b02efd2a983da82994a2e.jpg
It's the same nightmare Nala sees over and over. For the last time, she's seeing it again on the day of the experiment. The experiment that promises her a chance to erase that guilt, her trauma... her regret. To never see that nightmare again, once and for all.

But there is a difference. This time, in this dream, she has the chance to talk to the person in the mask... something that never happened in her dreams before.

notes.title: Dev Insights: The Book
notes.content:
The Book of Two Sons, and a Cursed Flower. In this instance, let's start with the Flower... shall we?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/859767ae0cdd1e16a68329671dae7e8193e7a43a.gif

For those who played our demo, the book may already be a familiar sight. After all, it's the first thing being shown in the game. As we approach the launch date, we'll get to open this book again, starting from the middle pages, in a chapter called Undying Flower.

The Concept Behind

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/dc9c70c2e21a64f7bca108dd8b2117883764d7f9.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/84f1e23a7db9411cff811953130cd6517a322072.png {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/0f627e35b2fb5eaa2eb9f88a2cdd066126a17cc6.png

Starting with this main concept, every following detail is then carefully thought of, from the cover to its content. The carnation in the water, the two suns surrounding it, and even the art on the pages inside the book aren’t there by chance. They're tied to the journey within the game. As for why we start from the middle pages, that is something you may or may not find eventually.

The book opens every time the game starts, and closes at the end of the story. Before it closes, it will react based on our journey throughout the game.

How will the book respond to yours?

notes.title: Dev Insights: Aurora
notes.content:
To express and visualize the surreal theme of Undying Flower, special effects play a crucial role.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/a2ba4689d940f42261bbe39d12fb01876795d998.png
One of the special effects that is shown a lot in many scenes is the Aurora effect. It represents the branches of memory that The Flower has seen during her journey.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/f3953f5d0c1f58ae26e74c7432403aa9fa298391.png
Aurora That Lives
We wanted the aurora's movement to feel alive. To achieve that, we created the effect using high poly mesh and a little bit of trigonometry to create the wavy movement with a controllable intensity. The intensity will dynamically change based on the music playing in the background.

[previewyoutube=ZZ4c_9Gi7UU;full][/previewyoutube]
The music sets the mood, and the aurora vibes with it.

notes.title: Dev Insights: The Memory World
notes.content:
The Flower has a unique ability: she can travel through people's memories. As she sees through someone's memory, her mind constructs a world known as the Memory World.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/2fc5f6857d76d0f61a9a50601356c5ee238ad991.png

It is originally just a blank space. But as she sees more memories, objects begin to appear. The room is designed to visualize how a person recalls memories. Objects tied to important moments are more likely to appear. They carry the stories and emotions of each moment. These key objects are called Memory Fragments.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/34b33309e65b3151edc1e21cc92199d3e5389dc0.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/2da02e41dbd30a583a9fd79aca0ef2bd7baea7a1.png

In real life, we don’t always remember where something was, but we remember how emotionally important it felt, and we definitely saw it in our memory. In Memory World, those objects are the ones floating above the room.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/c38cc2f1d6c59376e8846d3fd433f441e419d709.jpg

Each room has a different color based on the emotions the person felt in that moment. These moments are called Memory Points.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/5931acfc0fbebf36375bd85f69543f26742ee19c.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/85560d3489218800538e41788bf1f575e00a9796.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/b080d95a0fe149336a2f430e6a9b2d624a830292.jpg{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/557ff99e921f5b83af71dfc9406c59ae9bd5d8ec.png

In this game, we explore the memories of Nala as we find out the truth about her biggest regret of killing someone she loved.

notes.title: Dev Insights: The Mask
notes.content:
One of the most striking visuals in Undying Flower is the mask. It's the initial impression we kept hearing from some people playing our game. The mask is one of the biggest centerpieces of our visuals. It represents a true emotion that can only be shown in the world of memories owned by The Flower.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/4afb3646273156f45917d4ac828362c0ca2938a3.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/bc6f9740406b51e880d7decfe8b65715d02268fa.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/da4f76bf6dcb88282cce5e9103319a5229956b4d.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/fdb3afce00bac926dacc9ef986e966d422c7c049.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/589be8c252fae7c053fa4d3df596d69bea776bf6.png{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/274e35d7d27235f3607eff9e421c0ed4bf7e12a0.png

Design Inspiration
The design draws inspiration from the mask used in the Indonesian dance Tari Topeng, which literally translates to "Mask Dance." In this traditional performance, the mask conveys meaningful symbols through storytelling.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/11dd5025f2ff60325738ddf6309a62d51e617e44.jpg
Tari Topeng. (Kompas.com / Muhammad Irzal Adiakurnia)

In Undying Flower, the masks on character statues are latched to their faces with black substance that binds and rules them, showing us what emotions they are currently feeling.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/5736d8e76b49cc86e9092ab40caa57774d6d41b4.png

[hr][/hr]
In reality, a mask is usually used to cover real emotions. But in this world, the mask will show their heart.

notes.title: Where We Are & What's Next
notes.content:
Hi everyone! Since teaming up with our new publisher, indie.io, we've been able to push development further and improve the game with better standards. We are getting closer to delivering our full game, and we're happy to share our game progress, as well as sharing how we are going to move ahead.

Engine Upgrade
One of our biggest technical steps forward has been upgrading our game engine to Unity 2022. This resulted in several optimizations, better stability, better visuals, and most importantly: compatibility improvements, which may unlock more potentials for further upgrades in the future. It took some effort, but it was worth it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/1231afbbf6208e363d05bcff1b3109e6a3e3001b.png

Accessibility Improvements
Key rebindings will be available in full version release! We wanted to give you guys more flexibility in customizing controls to fit your preferences.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/d1fbaf2d526e3e4c2fb2d29673a2e2093dfb8664.png
We've heard your feedback as well regarding the UI navigation controls clarity, so we made a change to make them more intuitive and easier to navigate.

Ultrawide Support
We've also received some reports regarding the ultrawide issue, as it was not officially supported. Now, you can enjoy Undying Flower in ultrawide monitors, even in the demo version!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/f3953f5d0c1f58ae26e74c7432403aa9fa298391.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/4f564dd6b251b89e4568f2f7ce9c92860fa751c6.png

Improved English
Now that we got everything tied-up, we went for a full proofreading of our scripts. With the help of your feedback and our publisher, we have finally refined all of our English in-game texts!

[hr][/hr]
Moving Ahead
While there's still work to be done, it's definitely getting very close. Looking ahead, not only do we want to keep refining our game, but we also want to share more about the creative vision behind the game. We want to share the ideas and philosophies that shape Undying Flower, giving you a deeper context of what drives our design choices, in hope to build a stronger connection with you guys.

Stay tuned for more updates, and as always, thank you for your support! Don't forget to wishlist the game, and share!

notes.title: Official Publisher Announcement
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/0ee156745bda75b854fe4348683fcbfae3049bb4.png

We have a publisher!

We are very excited to announce that Calcatz has teamed with indie.io to bring Undying Flower to more gamers! 🎉🎉🎉

We have been working on Undying Flower for a long while and as a small team of 6 devs, this project has been massive. Having indie.io as a Publisher helps us get the game out there! They have a great track record of supporting a lot of indie games to reach more players and we believe that we can also learn so much from them to properly release this debut game of ours.

For those of you who may not know, working with a game publishing platform like indie.io greatly helps indie developers focus on game development while they handle all the behind-the-scenes magic. From helping manage store pages to crafting marketing campaigns and even helping the game shine at both digital and live events, indie.io helps in all the aspects that indie developers often struggle with alone.

We are very proud to have chosen them to publish our game, and very happy that they have chosen us.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45216987/0cede17850f39796081bd41fbda263fd1245612e.png

Thank you so much for your support throughout development so far!

This is a very proud and BIG moment for us, and we couldn’t have gotten to this point without all of you who supported us along the way 🤍 So we sincerely thank you and will keep working hard to be able to deliver the best storytelling experience that we can create in Undying Flower for all of you to enjoy!

For those of you who just got here, we welcome you to The Undying Flower 😁
